clue.text: Saw typical dog restrained by lead

indicators.note: being restrained by something means being held within it, so the dog goes inside the metal

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
Rover is the stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A saying about the typical dog kept on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash, but it is the metal, chemical symbol PB.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a proverb.

clue.text: Philanderer's surprised expression following drama

indicators.note: the exclamation comes after the drama, so it is placed second

parts.note: a play is a drama
Boy! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A womaniser exclaims in surprise after watching a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philanderer's' is the definition with 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy man devoted to pleasure and womanising is a philanderer.

clue.text: Something outstanding about rough outline

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a quarrel over money
a draft is a rough first version

explanation.surface: A remarkable feature of a rough sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' means unpaid, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn bank balance is a debt still owed, so something unpaid.

clue.text: Player occasionally making a run?

parts.note: reads as a cricketer who now and then scores, but means a film bit-part actor, or a cricket run not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: A batsman who only now and then manages to score a run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes and wides are runs credited to the side but not to any batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk-on film actor, or a run in cricket not scored off the bat: both senses fit.

clue.text: Analysis of mechanical failure

definitions.meaning: a detailed itemised analysis, as of costs
a car or machine ceasing to work

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a detailed itemised account of figures, and a vehicle or machine ceasing to work.

clue.text: Right treatment for a case — she's supposedly blind

definitions.meaning: fair treatment of a legal case is what courts aim to deliver
the statue of Lady ... is shown blindfolded to signify impartiality

explanation.surface: Fair handling of a court case, personified as a blindfolded woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness in a case is its sense of law; the personification is the blindfolded figure atop courthouses.

clue.text: Military group has a climbing expedition.

indicators.note: in a down clue a letter climbing moves up the column, toward the start of the word

parts.note: a junta is a military group ruling a country after a coup

explanation.surface: An army unit sets out on a mountaineering expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: In JUNTA the A rises from the bottom to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunt is a short pleasure trip or outing.

clue.text: Plan showing layers of rock and stone

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A geologist's diagram showing rock layers and a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning scheme or ruse is a plan.

clue.text: One takes over half of outlandish resort

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over the other, so the numeral comes first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only about half of the word is kept, so its final letters are dropped

parts.note: bizarre means outlandish

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of half of a weird holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the first four of BIZARRE's seven letters, rounding up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish Balearic island famous as a party holiday destination.

clue.text: Artist using paint, see, without a modification

indicators.note: a modification changes the form, so the letters of paint and see minus one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter uses paint and looks, but without changing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' removes A from PAINT SEE; the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor, so an artist.

clue.text: I may arrange to supply period books

parts.note: an age is a period of time
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone offering to provide books of a particular era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period books' reads as one phrase about historical volumes, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker or representative is someone who arranges supply on another's behalf.

clue.text: Royal staff require training in two points

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the rearranged letters sitting between the compass points

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters of the word require are rearranged

explanation.surface: Staff at the palace need instruction in a couple of matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'training' sits between east and south; 'in' places it there.
explanation.definitionFit: Equerries are officers attending members of the British royal family, so they are household staff.

clue.text: Retirement cover for person at the top

definitions.text: Retirement cover for person at the top

parts.words: Retirement cover for person at the top
parts.note: reads like insurance for an executive leaving office, but means a short garment worn over the upper body when sitting up in bed

explanation.surface: A pension scheme for a retiring chief executive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' is going to bed and 'person at the top' is the upper body, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A short warm garment worn over nightclothes on the upper half while sitting up in bed.

clue.text: Article about a new role for Macbeth?

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, so the definite article surrounds the following letters

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on a fresh part for an actor playing Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth is Thane of Glamis, then Cawdor, in Shakespeare's play; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth holds the Scottish noble title of thane in the play, a rank he plays out.

clue.text: Positive call — a run snatched — they eventually make centuries!

indicators.note: the positive call takes hold of the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: yes is a positive answer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A batsman calls yes, a run is grabbed, and centuries come in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (a 'century' is a hundred runs) misleads: centuries here are hundreds of years.
explanation.definitionFit: A century is a hundred of these units of time, so enough of them add up to centuries.

clue.text: It's wise to give way over bill, with promises to pay

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written above another comes first

parts.note: to sag is to give way or droop
AC is short for account, a bill
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: It is wise to give in on a bill when offered IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, perceptive and sound of judgement means wise.

clue.text: Having called in, anaesthetised an exotic creature

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, the telephoned word put within the unconscious one

parts.note: out means unconscious, as after an anaesthetic
rang means called on the phone

explanation.surface: After phoning the vet, someone sedated a strange animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having called' sounds like a sequence of events; it is just RANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape of Borneo and Sumatra is a creature exotic to most solvers.

clue.text: A useful thing when making charge, including small discount

indicators.note: one piece takes in another, so the word for small goes within

parts.note: a lance is the weapon a cavalryman uses when charging
low can mean small, as in a low number

explanation.surface: A handy thing when pricing up, including a small reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a price but is a cavalry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction allowed off the price is a discount.

clue.text: Use a keyboard to insert legal document into Melville's book

indicators.note: to insert one thing into another is to put it inside

parts.note: Typee is Herman Melville's first novel, set in the South Seas
a writ is a legal document

explanation.surface: Typing a writ into a Melville novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To typewrite is to produce text with a keyboard machine.

clue.text: Styling of a long coat, not short on sides

indicators.note: styling something gives it a new form, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor's description of fashioning a long coat that is not cut short at the sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not short on sides' reads as tailoring but means having plenty of sides, eight of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eight sides means a figure is well supplied with sides.

clue.text: Get around or possibly above it

indicators.note: possibly shows these letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Bypass something, or maybe go over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ABOVE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate a difficulty is to remove or avoid it, so to get round it.

clue.text: Clear away the mess made by second youngster

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky youngster

explanation.surface: The mess left behind by a second child needs clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to clean up spilt mess, finishing off a job.

clue.text: Type of flooring that's standard — noiseless one not required

parts.note: par means standard, as in up to par

indicators.note: one letter is not needed and so is removed from the quiet word

parts.note: quiet means noiseless
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A flooring that is standard, where quiet is not needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one not required' takes I from QUIET, giving QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooring of wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern is a type of floor.

clue.text: Very authoritative pronouncement, shortly, in old language

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter of the pronouncement is dropped

parts.note: an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: A very authoritative pronouncement, made briefly in an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims EDICT to EDIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The early form of Sanskrit used in the ancient Hindu scriptures is an old language.

clue.text: Small conflict in the outskirts of Dusseldorf

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the conflict going between the outskirts
outskirts are the edges of a city, so the first and last letters of the name

parts.note: a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A minor skirmish on the edge of Düsseldorf.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stunted or tiny is small.

clue.text: If pushed, one may turn blades against blades

definitions.text: If pushed, one may turn blades against blades

parts.words: If pushed, one may turn blades against blades
parts.note: sounds like a reluctant swordsman fighting back, but describes a garden machine whose rotating cutters slice through grass

explanation.surface: A swordsman, if pressed, might cross swords with an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The first blades are cutting edges; the second are blades of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden machine, often pushed by hand, with rotating cutters that trim grass.

clue.text: Northern VIP put in position to host monarch?

indicators.note: a host holds a guest within, so the monarch goes inside

parts.note: laid means put down in place
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A Scottish dignitary placed so as to entertain a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern means Scottish here: a laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish landowner of standing is a northern personage of importance.

clue.text: I had radio buff turn up Messiah

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the pieces from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: A radio enthusiast confesses to tuning in to Handel's Messiah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses IDHAM. Messiah in italics hints at Handel; it is the Islamic redeemer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam the Mahdi is the prophesied redeemer, a messianic figure.

clue.text: Strong woman's in a muddle, mostly to do with Scotsman

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so the last letter of the muddle is dropped

parts.note: a maze is a confusing tangle, a muddle
on means concerning or to do with
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A powerful woman finds herself confused about a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MAZE to MAZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a mythical race of warrior women, so the adjective describes a powerful woman.

clue.text: Quartet of Tchaikovsky's you heard? What poetry!'.

indicators.note: a quartet is a group of four, so four consecutive letters are taken from inside the composer's name
heard points to how the word sounds when spoken, giving a single letter

parts.note: the word you is said exactly like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone hears a Tchaikovsky string quartet and exclaims at its poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quartet' suggests a string quartet but means four letters, HAIK, from inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese verse form of seventeen syllables, so a kind of poetry, as the exclamation says.

clue.text: Some of side suffering reverses given out

indicators.note: reverses tells us the run of letters taken is read backwards
only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside its words

explanation.surface: One side in a contest suffers setbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: DESUFFE runs across 'side suffering'; 'reverses' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To effuse is to pour out or emit, so this past form means poured or sent out.

clue.text: Obvious occasion to hide basic instincts

indicators.note: something hidden is kept inside, so the instincts go within the occasion

parts.note: an event is an occasion
in Freudian psychology the id is the part of the mind holding basic instincts

explanation.surface: An obvious opportunity to cover up primal urges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain to see is clear and apparent.
